messages:
Ravi K: Heads-up: I started a tiny PR to clarify autoscale UX wording and add a short CLI + SDK snippet for tenant isolation labels. Link: https://go/repo/pr/4599
Joanne P: Nice. Can you call out that p99 targets are 'steady-state' and not including scale transient? We keep getting support tickets on that.
Ravi K: Yep planning to change the SLA row to 'p99 (steady-state): target 40ms' and add a parenthetical note about transient increases during scale events.
Theo Eng: For the isolation label example, customers often try `isolation=dedicated` which doesn't do what they expect. Suggest using `tenant:isolation=reserved` and explain what reserved actually buys you.
Ravi K: Good catch. I'll add a short bullet: "tenant:isolation=reserved -> avoids eviction by autoscaler; not a capacity guarantee."
Maya: Also mention eviction order when capacity pressure occurs (best-effort preemption list first, then burst tenants). Short line is enough.
Ravi K: Will add. Thinking of adding an example CLI command for setting labels:
```bash
redwood-cli tenants update t-99 --label tenant:isolation=reserved
```
Joanne P: Ooh can we also include a tiny curl/HTTP SDK example? People search docs for that often.
Ravi K: Sure, I'll add both curl + node snippet.
Theo Eng: For the node snippet include error handling for 409 (conflict) if they try to set a policy that already exists.
Ravi K: Added a node snippet in the draft:
```js
const {Dedicated} = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Dedicated({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY});
try {
  await client.tenants.updateLabels('t-99', { 'tenant:isolation': 'reserved' });
} catch (err) {
  if (err.status === 409) console.warn('Label update conflict, retry or contact support');
  else throw err;
}
```
infra-bot: Note: cross-link to /docs/dedicated/eviction-behavior is recommended (found via handbook search).
Ravi K: Added link to eviction-behavior doc and a one-line summary. Thanks infra-bot.
Joanne P: Tiny nit: change wording "avoid eviction" -> "reduces eviction likelihood".
Ravi K: Done. Also reworked the autoscale YAML example to show interplay between targetUtilization and burst mode:
```yaml
autoscale:
  policies:
    - id: stable
      mode: stable
      min: 2
      max: 20
      targetUtilization: 0.6
      cooldown: 600
    - id: burst
      mode: burst
      max: 100
      cooldown: 120
```
Maya: Can you add a note that burst may increase p99 and to test with synthetic traffic?
Ravi K: Yep added a short callout and a link to the perf-test repo.
Docs Bot: Preview build succeeded: https://go/docs-preview/4599. Rendering includes snippets.
Joanne P: LGTM from docs POV. One last ask: include a brief 'migration path' blurb for tenants that used the old label `reserved=true`.
Ravi K: Good idea. I added a migration example and a CLI one-liner for bulk update.
Theo Eng: Approved. Go ahead and merge once CI green. Also maybe follow up with a short tweet about the clearer docs elsewhere? :slightly_smiling_face:
Ravi K: Merging now. Will follow up with a short changelog note and a slack blurb in #product. Thanks all.
Docs Bot: PR merged  live: https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/autoscale-ux-clarify (may take a minute to propagate)
